# STM32H743 FC + 4-in-1 ESC Stack (Job #26): Power, Thermal, and DShot Architecture

I don't have prior Job #26 documents (BOM, stackup, MOSFET selection), so this is a parameterized model with explicit assumptions. Substitute datasheet values where marked. All equations hold regardless of the specific parts.

**Architectural note:** The STM32H743 runs ArduPilot and generates bidirectional DShot600. The 48 kHz PWM is generated by each ESC's own MCU (AM32 or BLHeli_32, e.g. STM32G071 or AT32F421), not by the H743. The netlist splits along that boundary.

---

## 0. Baseline Assumptions

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bus voltage (6S, full) | V_bus | 25.2 V | worst-case switching |
| Burst phase current per motor | I_ph | 80 A | spec |
| PWM frequency | f_sw | 48 kHz | spec |
| MOSFET R_DS(on) @ 25 °C, V_GS=10 V | R₂₅ | 1.2 mΩ | **assumed** 5×6 / 3.3×3.3 PQFN, 40 V class |
| R_DS(on) temperature coefficient | α | ≈ 0.0055 /K (gives ×1.55 at 125 °C) | typical trench |
| Total switching transition | t_r + t_f | 40 ns | layout-limited, **verify on scope** |
| Dead time | t_dt | 200 ns per edge | ESC firmware setting |
| Body-diode V_F @ 80 A | V_F | 0.8 V | **assumed** |
| Reverse recovery charge | Q_rr | 50 nC | **assumed** |
| Total gate charge | Q_g | 50 nC | **assumed** |
| Gate drive voltage | V_drv | 10 V | FD6288-class driver |
| Commutation | — | 6-step trapezoidal, complementary (synchronous) PWM | AM32/BLHeli_32 default |

**Reality check:** 80 A sustained phase current on a 20×20 or 30×30 board is not thermally possible (shown below). "80 A burst" must be bounded in time, and Section 3 derives that bound.

---

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Current paths (6-step, complementary PWM)

In each 60° electrical sector, two phases are active:

- **PWM leg:** the high-side (HS) FET conducts for D·T_sw. The low-side (LS) FET of the same leg freewheels for (1−D)·T_sw (synchronous rectification).
- **Static leg:** its LS FET conducts 100 % of the sector.

So at any instant, current I_ph passes through exactly **two** FET channels in series:

$$P_{cond,bridge}(T_j) = 2\,I_{ph}^2\,R_{DS(on)}(T_j)\quad\text{(independent of }D\text{)}$$

$$R_{DS(on)}(T_j) = R_{25}\left[1+\alpha\,(T_j-25)\right]$$

Each FET is active for 120° of 360° (1/3 of the electrical period). The HS/LS split depends on D, but the average per FET is:

$$\overline{P}_{cond,FET} = \frac{2 I_{ph}^2 R_{DS}}{6} = \frac{I_{ph}^2 R_{DS}}{3}$$

The worst-case single FET is the LS at low D: within a sector it carries the static-leg role or the freewheel (1−D) role.

$$P_{cond,LS,max} \approx \frac{I_{ph}^2 R_{DS}}{3}\cdot\frac{1+(1-D)}{2}\cdot 2 \;\xrightarrow{D\to 0}\; \tfrac{2}{3}I_{ph}^2R_{DS}\text{ (peak sector-weighted)}$$

| T_j | R_DS(on) | P_cond per bridge (motor) | Avg per FET |

| 25 °C | 1.20 mΩ | 15.4 W | 2.56 W |
| 100 °C | 1.70 mΩ | 21.8 W | 3.63 W |
| 125 °C | 1.86 mΩ | 23.8 W | 3.97 W |
